subject: On-prem deployment: cluster sizing, node-pool mapping & block storage notes
messages:
From: Alice Moss <alice.moss@ironridge.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private deploy planning kickoff — site constraints and storage Qs

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is ready to move into an on-prem planning cadence. We're the operations lead at IronRidge. We have three hosting sites (primary DC in Austin, warm standby in Columbus, and dev in Phoenix). Before we book a deep-dive we wanted to share a couple of constraints so your sizing proposal can reflect reality: 

- Storage: primary site has 8TB local NVMe per server (RAID0-like ephemeral use only) and a central SAN (iSCSI LUNs served by two controllers) for persistent model artifacts.
- Network: limited routed VLANs, public egress via single ASN with existing BGP sessions; we can provision VLANs but prefer minimal changes.
- Security: Data-at-rest encryption enforced via customer KMS (HSM-backed) and limited outbound access from pods.
- Compliance: logs must be retained for 90 days and exported to our SIEM; SOC2 reports available upon request.

Questions:
1) How do you recommend mapping node pools for workload isolation (model serving vs batched offline eval vs admin tasks)?
2) For model weights larger than 50GB, do you recommend local NVMe caching + SAN for persistence or a blockstore mount per node?
3) Any preference between Rook-Ceph vs Longhorn for block PVs given the SAN presence?

I've attached a spreadsheet with our rough CPU/GPU counts and the site network diagram. Can your team give a quick outline of recommended node types and the trade-offs?

Thanks,
Alice Moss
Ops Lead, IronRidge Analytics
alice.moss@ironridge.com
From: priyom.das@redwood.ai <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Moss <alice.moss@ironridge.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 13:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy planning kickoff — site constraints and storage Qs

Alice — thanks for the detail and the attachments. High level answers below; we'll follow up with a short design doc and a one-hour technical review next week. I've attached a preliminary sizing workbook that maps your supplied counts to node profiles.

Short answers up front:
- Node-pool mapping: 3 logical pools recommended — serving (GPU backed), batch/encode (CPU optimized, burstable), and infra (control-plane + storage gateway + logging). This keeps KV cache sizing and eviction behaviors isolated.
- Storage pattern for >50GB models: use local NVMe as a hot cache (ephemeral) for model shards + SAN LUN mounted by a small set of stateful gateway pods (read-through caching). Avoid mounting SAN LUNs directly on every inference node to reduce iSCSI session scale and to keep model lifecycle simpler.
- Rook-Ceph vs Longhorn: given you already have a central SAN, prefer Longhorn for small controller-managed PVs and worker-local ephemerals for NVMe. Rook-Ceph adds operational overhead unless you need multi-site replication or object semantics.

Trade-offs and notes:
- Latency: local NVMe hot-caching reduces cold-starts for KV/cache by 5–20ms per request in our benchmarks.
- Cost: fewer iSCSI sessions equals less SAN licensing and simpler multipath configs.
- HA: run 3 storage gateway replicas across availability racks at primary site; use async replication to standby for DR.

Next steps:
1) Marissa will propose a concrete node size matrix (vCPU, memory, GPU type, local NVMe claim) and a proposed PV strategy.
2) Karthik will draft the network segmentation plan (VLANs, BGP peering notes, egress routes).
3) We'll schedule the review — propose Tue/Wed next week.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai

Attachments: ironridge-prelim-sizing.xlsx (spreadsheet), site-network-diagram_v1.pdf (diagram)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai, Alice Moss <alice.moss@ironridge.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy planning kickoff — node types + storage gateway proposal

Hi team — following Priyom's note I've sketched a node-pool matrix and a checklist for the technical review. Key proposals below (see attached proposal-checklist.md for full context):

1) Node pools (logical):
   - gpu-serving-pool: 8–16 GPUs per node (A100/RTX depending on customer preference), 1.5–2 TB memory for large KV caches, 2 x 4TB NVMe (RAID0 for speed; data ephemeral)
   - cpu-batch-pool: dense vCPU (48–96 vCPU), 512–768 GB RAM, 2 x 1TB NVMe for local caching of batched artifacts
   - infra-pool: 3 control-plane nodes (taints to prevent workloads), 3 storage-gateway pods (statefulset with anti-affinity), 2 logging/metrics replicas (Fluentd -> SIEM)

2) Storage gateway pattern:
   - Small pool of gateway pods (stateful) mounts SAN LUNs (iSCSI) via a multipath configuration; gateway exposes models to local nodes via NFS or a CSI-proxy. Avoid mounting the LUN across all nodes.
   - Gateways handle model lifecycle (pre-fetch, eviction heuristics) and expose an HTTP fetch endpoint for model servers to pull shards into local NVMe.

3) CSI and replication choices:
   - Use Longhorn for persistent small-block PVs that back critical services (consistency on controller); rely on SAN snapshots for full-model archival backups.
   - If you later require cross-site promotion of models, we can add Rook Object for replica sets, but keep it optional.

4) Network and routing notes (Karthik's input to follow):
   - Dedicate two VLANs for model egress and control-plane management.
   - BGP peering retained as-is; provision static routes for cluster-to-gateway path and ensure MTU 9000 for NVMe over fabrics where used.

Ask for review: please confirm whether SAN LUNs are presented with multi-tenant export policies or per-app LUNs; that affects gateway scale. Also confirm whether you can provision a dedicated VLAN for model-pull traffic.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Marissa / Priyom — this is very helpful and addresses most of our concerns. Quick answers: 

- SAN exports: we can carve per-app LUNs; I'll confirm exact number with storage team (likely 6 LUNs to start).
- VLAN: we can provision a dedicated VLAN for model-pull traffic and will enable jumbo frames on the switch fabric in Austin.

Next steps per IronRidge:
1) I'll confirm LUN counts and share NFS export policies by EOD Wednesday.
2) Please send a short runbook for the gateway multipath configuration and a recommended readiness probe for the gateway pod.
3) Schedule the technical review: Tue 16th at 10am CST works for my team.

We are okay proceeding with the Longhorn-first approach; we'll revisit Rook if multi-site replication becomes a hard requirement. Thanks for calling out the eviction heuristics — that was a major internal ask.

Best,
Alice Moss
Ops Lead, IronRidge Analytics
